artifacts.summary: Traces the operator parsing/registration pipeline and finds the parser is already Unicode-agnostic for infix/prefix operators; the real gap is that Operator.name is a single string with no alias slot, so operators.py cannot expose both a canonical LaTeX name and a user-chosen Unicode glyph for the same operator class. Recommends adding an Operator.aliases class attribute plus an OperatorCollection.add_operator extension, scoped to arity-1/arity-2 operators (excludes \top/\bot).

next_steps: Run /plan 220 to create an implementation plan for the Operator.aliases mechanism

memory_candidates.content: In ModelChecker, the formula parser (utils/parsing.py, syntactic/collection.py, syntactic/sentence.py) is already fully generic with respect to operator-name spelling: arbitrary Unicode strings work today as Operator.name for both infix (arity-2) and prefix (arity-1) operators, with no changes needed to the parser itself. The only hardcoded-by-literal-string operators are the two nullary constants \top/\bot, which are matched by literal string comparison at 8+ call sites across syntactic/ and theory_lib/. The syntactic/tests/unit/test_operators.py and test_syntax.py fixtures already use Unicode operator names ("∧", "∨", "¬") as their default test data, proving this generic behavior.

In ModelChecker, OperatorCollection.add_operator (syntactic/collection.py) always keys its operator_dictionary from the operator class's own `.name` class attribute, discarding any dict keys a caller's get_operators() function used. This means an operator can only ever be looked up under one spelling today; giving a theory operator both a LaTeX name and a Unicode alias requires a new `aliases` class-attribute mechanism, not just adding extra entries to a get_operators() dict (those extra dict keys are silently ignored when the values are registered via add_operator).

ModelChecker already has two separate, working-but-disconnected Unicode<->LaTeX operator translation mechanisms that are NOT wired into the core syntactic parser: (1) jupyter/unicode.py's latex_to_unicode/unicode_to_latex static dicts plus the theory extension point UNICODE_OPERATOR_EXTENSIONS (only implemented by exclusion/__init__.py), used solely for Jupyter notebook display; (2) semantic_theory["dictionary"] consumed by builder/translation.py's OperatorTranslation.translate, a naive pre-parse str.replace() substitution used only for theory-to-theory operator translation (e.g. exclusion->logos for --maximize). Neither affects the model-checker CLI's actual formula parsing of a single theory's own notation.
